BudgetDeclared.description:
The budget a receipt declares (ADR-024 §8). Enforcement is a separate issue, and this type says
so: there is no `enforced` here to set to `true`.

DeclaredEffect.description: An effect a step declares it may produce.

content_digests.description: The digest the content at each path must have afterwards, parallel to `paths`.

Expectation.description: What a step must meet to count as having done its job.

description.description: What is expected, in words the operator can read back.

quality_level.description: The quality level this step is expected to establish, when it establishes one.

QualityClaim.description:
A quality level **and whose claim it is** (ADR-024 §2 D1).

On a receipt the source is always `Caller`: nothing has run yet. The field exists on the receipt
rather than being implied, so the attestation can echo it without inventing one.

source.description: Always `Caller` here — a receipt is a declaration.

QualityLevel.description:
Four-tier escalation of test scope, from narrowest to broadest.

Each level represents a progressively broader scope of validation:
- `TargetedTests`: only tests directly relevant to the change
- `Package`: all tests in the affected crate/package
- `Workspace`: all tests across the entire workspace
- `MergeReady`: workspace + all integration gates (lint, format, audit)

The levels implement `PartialOrd`/`Ord` so contracts can check
`observed >= required` for satisfaction.

oneOf.description:
Only tests directly relevant to the change passed.
E.g., `cargo test -p crate -- specific::test`

The crate/package tests passed.
E.g., `cargo test -p crate`

Full workspace tests passed.
E.g., `cargo test --workspace`

Workspace + all integration gates (lint, format, audit) passed.
E.g., full CI pipeline.

depends_on.description: The steps it depends on, by id.

id.description: The step's id, unique within the receipt.

requires_approval.description: Whether a human must approve it first.

Sandbox.description:
The sandbox a step runs in. `none` is deliberately not representable (ADR-024 §4): a receipt
that declares no isolation cannot be written, so a host cannot ask for an unisolated run by
omitting a field.

image_digest.description: The image the regime resolves to.

SandboxRegime.description: The sandbox regimes this engine implements.

Workspace.description:
What identifies a workspace (ADR-024 §5).

The identity carries its own `kind` so a decision that is not taken cannot be smuggled in as a
string: `CommitTree` ships, and a dirty-tree identity later is an additive vocabulary value that
an old reader refuses, rather than a schema break.

value.description: The identity itself — for `CommitTree`, `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`.

WorkspaceKind.description: The workspace kinds this engine implements. Closed vocabulary, unknown = refuse.

oneOf.description: A commit tree OID. The only kind 1.15.0 accepts.

description: The declaration a host writes before an execution (ADR-024 §4). The engine parses it with `Receipt::from_document`, verifies it against the workspace identity it computed, and refuses it with the variants named in `ReceiptRefusal`.

execution_id.description: The execution this receipt is for — one receipt, one execution (§5's resume half is #1528's).

fixture_digests.description: The digests of the fixtures the execution reads.

quality_required.description: The quality level the caller claims it needs, **as a claim**.

sandbox.description: The sandbox its steps run in.

schema_version.description: The schema version, first in the canonical bytes.

set_digest.description: The digest over the declared effect set, for a caller that pins one separately.

steps.description:
Its steps.

There is no `roles` field (#1586): a signed field with no producer, no reader and no `source:`
is a contract nobody keeps, and if a host filled it the engine would sign two of its values it
cannot observe. Roles belong to the harness (ADR-024 §11).
